deck_surface_input_groups.description: Deck has multiple component types with different UOMs. Floor is SF-based, railings are LF-based, spindles and stairs are EA-based. Engine divides quantity by rate to calculate hours.

task_production_rates.name: Siding Protection at Deck-to-House Junction
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Mask siding at ledger board junction with plastic sheeting taped at top edge, 4-6 ft height coverage. ~36 sec per LF. Includes taping top edge, securing bottom, and ensuring no gaps at ledger board transition. LF of house wall along deck edge.

defect_tolerance.all: Full coverage of siding face from deck level up 4-6 ft. Plastic secured at top and bottom. No gaps at ledger board transition.

task_production_rates.name: Landscape Protection Below Deck
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Deploy tarps and plastic sheeting below elevated deck to protect vegetation from stain drip-through between deck boards. ~18 sec per SF. Includes staking at grade. Conditional on elevated deck with landscape below.

defect_tolerance.all: Full coverage below deck footprint. Tarps secured against wind. No gaps where stain could drip through to plantings.

task_production_rates.name: Hardscape Protection Adjacent to Deck
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Lay drop cloths on adjacent walkways, patios, and concrete at deck perimeter. ~14 sec per SF. Protects from stain overspray and drip during application. Same rate as masonry hardscape protection.

defect_tolerance.all: Full coverage of adjacent hardscape within overspray zone. Drop cloths secured at edges.

task_production_rates.name: Deck Furniture Staging and Relocation
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Move all on-deck furniture, planters, grills, and accessories off deck surface or consolidate under tarps in non-working zone. ~30 min average. Highly variable by deck size and furniture count. Includes covering items that cannot be relocated.

defect_tolerance.all: All items relocated or covered. Clear working surface. No items in staining path.

task_production_rates.name: Deck Fixture Masking
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Bag and tape deck-mounted and railing-mounted light fixtures with plastic and blue tape. ~8-9 min per fixture. Deck fixtures often at post cap or railing level — straightforward access. Slightly slower than interior fixtures due to outdoor tape adhesion variability.

defect_tolerance.all: All fixtures fully bagged and sealed. Tape edges secure. No exposed glass or lens surfaces.

task_production_rates.name: Deck Moisture Content Testing
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Pin-type moisture meter readings across deck floor surface at multiple points. MC >15% for PT pine or >12% for cedar/redwood is HARD STOP. ~20 min for standard deck (multiple test points per zone). Mandatory for ALL wood conditions. Includes documentation of readings.

defect_tolerance.all: Multiple test points across deck surface documented. All readings below threshold. Wet spots flagged for re-test.

task_production_rates.name: Seasoning Period Verification
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Verify pressure-treated wood seasoning period from install date. PT pine requires 2-4 weeks (ACQ treatment) to 3-6 months seasoning before coating. Check for water beading on surface (indicates preservative still at surface). Administrative verification + water sprinkle test. ~12 min.

defect_tolerance.all: Install date verified. Water absorption test performed. Seasoning period confirmed adequate.

task_production_rates.name: Mill Glaze Removal Sanding
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Aggressive sanding with 60-grit to remove mill glaze from new lumber surfaces. ~72 sec per SF. Mill glaze is the burnished surface from kiln drying and planing that prevents stain penetration. Belt sander or random orbital with aggressive grit. Mandatory for new milled wood. Creates open grain for stain absorption.

defect_tolerance.all: All mill glaze removed. Water droplet test shows immediate absorption (no beading). Uniform open grain across entire surface.

task_production_rates.name: Deck Floor Refinishing Sand
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Refinishing sand with 80-100 grit for previously coated or weathered deck surfaces. ~72 sec per SF. Removes loose/flaking coating, smooths raised grain on weathered wood, and creates profile for new coating. Belt sander or random orbital. Rate same as mill glaze sand — different grit but similar effort.

defect_tolerance.all: All loose coating removed. Raised grain smoothed. Uniform surface profile. No deep gouges from sanding.

task_production_rates.name: Deck Floor Pressure Wash
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Pressure wash deck floor surface at 1,000-1,500 PSI (wood-safe pressure). ~9 sec per SF. Removes dirt, mildew, gray weathered wood fiber, and chemical residue from stripping. Fan tip, maintain 12-18 inch distance. 24-48 hr dry time after (not included in rate). Use after chemical restoration or as standalone prep for weathered decks.

defect_tolerance.all: Uniform clean surface. No gray weathered fiber remaining. No pressure damage or furring. Even pressure pattern — no striping.

task_production_rates.name: Mildew Treatment
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Apply mildew treatment solution (sodium hypochlorite or oxygen bleach), allow dwell time, scrub with stiff brush, rinse. ~24 sec per SF. Required when visible mildew or algae is present. Horizontal wood decks are prone to mildew in shaded or humid areas. Treatment must kill mildew spores to prevent growth under new coating.

defect_tolerance.all: All visible mildew eliminated. Surface passes bleach test (no dark spots returning within 15 minutes). No residue remaining.

task_production_rates.name: Railing System Sanding
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Hand sand railing system (top rail, bottom rail, posts) per linear foot of railing run. ~5 min per LF. Complex profile — multiple surfaces per LF (top, sides, underside of top rail; posts at intervals). 80-100 grit for weathered/previously coated, 60 grit for new mill glaze. Significantly slower than flat floor sanding due to profile complexity and hand work.

defect_tolerance.all: All railing surfaces sanded to uniform profile. No glossy spots remaining. Posts and rail undersides included.

task_production_rates.name: Spindle/Baluster Sanding
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Hand sand individual spindles/balusters — all 4 sides plus top and bottom transitions. ~5 min per spindle. Turned spindles are slower (complex profile); square spindles faster. Rate reflects mixed average. 80-100 grit hand sand with folded paper.

defect_tolerance.all: All spindle surfaces sanded. No glossy spots. Top and bottom transitions included. Turned profiles followed.

task_production_rates.name: Railing System Wash
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Wash railing system with garden hose or low-pressure wash (NOT high-pressure — too close to wood detail). ~2 min per LF. Remove sanding dust, dirt, chemical residue. Includes spindles within railing run. Lower pressure than floor wash to protect detail profiles.

defect_tolerance.all: All railing surfaces clean. No sanding dust or chemical residue. Spindles rinsed. Allow dry time.

task_production_rates.name: Chemical Stripper Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Apply alkaline deck stripper by pump sprayer or brush. ~13 sec per SF. Even coverage required for uniform stripping. Work in manageable sections to maintain wet edge. Part of 3-step chemical restoration for weathered wood.

defect_tolerance.all: Even application across entire surface. No dry spots. Maintained wet edge. Working sections clearly defined.

task_production_rates.name: Stripper Dwell Time
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Allow chemical stripper to dwell on surface per manufacturer specification. ~15-20 min depending on product. Crew monitors for drying (re-wet if needed). No active labor but crew on-site. Fixed time per application cycle.

defect_tolerance.all: Dwell time per manufacturer spec. Surface kept wet throughout dwell period. No premature drying.

task_production_rates.name: Stripper Agitation/Scrub
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Scrub stripper into surface with stiff bristle brush or deck scrub brush on pole. ~24 sec per SF. Agitates chemical into wood grain and loosens old coating. Labor-intensive — requires physical pressure. Work same sections as application.

defect_tolerance.all: All sections scrubbed uniformly. Old coating visibly loosening. No skipped areas.

task_production_rates.name: Stripper Rinse
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Pressure rinse stripped surface at 1,000-1,500 PSI to remove chemical residue and loosened coating. ~9 sec per SF. Fan tip, maintain distance. Thorough rinse is critical — residual stripper will prevent stain adhesion.

defect_tolerance.all: All chemical residue removed. No stripper film remaining. Clean wood surface visible. Water runs clear.

task_production_rates.name: Wood Brightener Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Apply acid-based wood brightener (oxalic acid for cedar/redwood, citric acid alternative) by pump sprayer. ~13 sec per SF. Neutralizes alkaline stripper, restores natural wood color, opens grain. Same application rate as stripper — pump sprayer coverage. For cedar/redwood: also neutralizes tannin staining.

defect_tolerance.all: Even application across entire surface. No dry spots. Wood color visibly brightening within minutes.

task_production_rates.name: Brightener Dwell Time
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Allow wood brightener to dwell per manufacturer spec. ~10-15 min. Shorter dwell than stripper. Crew monitors for even color change. Fixed time per application cycle.

defect_tolerance.all: Dwell time per manufacturer spec. Uniform color change visible. No premature rinse.

task_production_rates.name: Brightener Rinse
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Pressure rinse brightened surface at 1,000-1,500 PSI. ~9 sec per SF. Remove all chemical residue. Same rate as stripper rinse. 24-48 hr dry time required before staining (not included in rate).

defect_tolerance.all: All brightener residue removed. Wood shows natural color. No chemical film remaining. Surface pH neutral.

task_production_rates.name: Post-Wash Dry Verification
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Verify deck surface has dried to acceptable MC after washing or chemical restoration. Pin-type moisture meter check at multiple points. Confirm MC below threshold (15% PT pine, 12% cedar/redwood). ~12 min for standard deck. May require return visit if not dry (24-48 hr dry time after chemical restoration).

defect_tolerance.all: All test points below MC threshold. No visible wet spots. Surface ready for stain application.

task_production_rates.name: Deck Floor Stain — Spray + Back-Brush (Coat 1)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Airless spray stain onto deck floor followed immediately by back-brushing to work stain into wood grain. 275 SF/hr per 2-person crew-hour (sprayer + brusher). Back-brushing is MANDATORY for penetrating stains — spray alone does not force stain into grain. Spray/backbrush coupling: spray rate (275) <= backbrush rate (275) — compliant. Maintain wet edge across boards. Work with grain direction.

defect_tolerance.all: Even penetration across all boards. No pooling between boards. Back-brushed within 30 seconds of spray. Consistent color. No dry edges.

task_production_rates.name: Deck Floor Stain — Brush Application (Coat 1)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush-only stain application on deck floor. ~29 sec per SF. 4-inch stain brush, work with grain, maintain wet edge board-by-board. Excellent penetration but slow. Primary method for small decks, tight areas, or when spray is not feasible. Single worker.

defect_tolerance.all: Even penetration. No brush marks visible after absorption. Consistent color board to board. Wet edge maintained.

task_production_rates.name: Deck Floor Stain — Pad Applicator (Coat 1)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Lamb's wool pad or stain pad applicator on extension pole for deck floor. ~14 sec per SF. Good penetration with faster coverage than brush. Best for large flat deck areas. Single worker on pole. Maintain wet edge.

defect_tolerance.all: Even application. No pad marks or streaking after absorption. Consistent coverage. Wet edge maintained.

task_production_rates.name: Deck Floor Stain — Roller Application (Coat 1)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Roller application of stain on deck floor using 3/8 to 1/2 inch nap roller on extension pole. ~18 sec per SF. Faster than brush but less grain penetration — best for solid stains where film-build matters more than penetration. Back-brush roller laps if penetrating stain. Single worker.

defect_tolerance.all: Even coverage. No roller marks after drying. Consistent film build for solid stains. No pooling between boards.

task_production_rates.name: Deck Floor Stain — Second Coat
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Second coat uses same method and rate as coat 1. Rate shown is spray_backbrush baseline — actual rate follows selected application_method from coat 1. First coat seals grain, so second coat sits on a more consistent surface. Same production rate — penetrating stains still require back-brushing on second coat to avoid surface pooling.

defect_tolerance.all: Even coverage over first coat. No pooling or runs. Consistent color depth. Maintain wet edge.

task_production_rates.name: Railing Stain — Spray + Back-Brush (Coat 1)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Spray stain on railing system (top rail, bottom rail, posts) followed by back-brushing into grain. 12 LF/hr per 2-person crew-hour. ~5 min per LF. Multiple surfaces per LF — top, sides, undersides. Back-brushing mandatory for penetrating stains. Spray/backbrush coupling compliant.

defect_tolerance.all: All railing surfaces coated — top, sides, undersides. Posts fully coated. Back-brushed into grain. No runs on vertical post faces.

task_production_rates.name: Railing Stain — Brush Application (Coat 1)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush-only stain application on railing system. ~6 min per LF. 2-3 inch brush for rails and posts. Multiple surfaces per LF. Good penetration. Primary method for most deck railings. Single worker.

defect_tolerance.all: All surfaces coated. No brush marks after absorption. Posts and rail undersides included. No runs.

task_production_rates.name: Spindle Stain — Spray Application (Coat 1)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Spray stain on individual spindles/balusters — all 4 sides. ~4 min per spindle. Spray is faster than brush for spindles — spray from multiple angles to coat all sides. Back-brush not practical on individual spindles (spray coats all sides simultaneously). Turned spindles slower, square faster — rate is mixed average.

defect_tolerance.all: All 4 sides coated. Top and bottom transitions covered. No drips or runs. Even color.

task_production_rates.name: Spindle Stain — Brush Application (Coat 1)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush stain on individual spindles — all 4 sides plus top/bottom transitions. ~6 min per spindle. 2-inch brush. Tedious hand work — each spindle is a small project. Turned profiles are slower. Single worker.

defect_tolerance.all: All surfaces coated including transitions. No brush marks after absorption. Even color. No drips.

task_production_rates.name: Railing Stain — Second Coat
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Second coat on railing system. Same rate as coat 1. Rate shown is spray_backbrush baseline — actual rate follows selected application_method. First coat seals grain for more consistent second coat.

defect_tolerance.all: Even coverage over first coat. Consistent color depth. No runs on posts. All surfaces covered.

task_production_rates.name: Spindle Stain — Second Coat
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Second coat on spindles. Same rate as coat 1. Rate shown is spray baseline — actual rate follows selected application_method.

defect_tolerance.all: Even coverage over first coat. Consistent color depth on all sides. No drips.

task_production_rates.name: Stair Step Stain — Brush Application (Coat 1)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush stain on individual stair steps (tread + riser per step). ~20 min per step. Alternating step pattern — stain every other step to maintain access, allow to dry, then do remaining steps. Includes end-grain sealing on exposed tread edges. End grain absorbs heavily — requires extra stain and care. 3 EA/hr midpoint.

defect_tolerance.all: Full coverage on tread and riser. End grain sealed with extra coat. Alternating pattern maintained for access. No pooling at tread/riser junction.

task_production_rates.name: Stair Step Stain — Second Coat
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Second coat on stair steps. Same rate as coat 1. Same alternating step pattern. End grain may need third spot-coat (not included — edge case).

defect_tolerance.all: Even coverage over first coat. End grain fully sealed. Consistent color. Alternating pattern maintained.

task_production_rates.name: Final Walkthrough Inspection
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Walk entire deck surface inspecting for holidays, uneven color, missed spots, drips on railings, pooling between boards. Check all components — floor, railings, spindles, stairs. ~20 min for standard deck. Includes solid stain delamination risk documentation when coating_type = solid_stain.

defect_tolerance.all: Complete visual inspection of all stained surfaces. No missed spots. Color consistency verified. Railing drips checked. Solid stain: no bubbling or delamination signs.

task_production_rates.name: Touch-Up Staining
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush touch-up of defects found during final inspection. ~48 sec per SF. Rate is per total floor SF — most area passes without touch-up. Includes spot re-staining of holidays, evening out color variations, and re-coating any sanded/scraped drip areas on railings.

defect_tolerance.all: All defects repaired. Touch-ups blended into surrounding stain. No visible repair boundaries after drying.

task_production_rates.name: Furniture Return and Repositioning
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Return all furniture, planters, grills, and accessories to original positions on cured deck surface. ~22 min average. Slightly faster than staging (no covering/tarping needed). Must verify deck surface is dry to touch before placing furniture.

defect_tolerance.all: All items returned to original positions. No damage to fresh stain from dragging. Surface verified dry before placement.

task_production_rates.name: Protection Material Removal
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove all protection materials — siding plastic, landscape tarps, hardscape covers, fixture bags. ~20 min. Check for tape residue on siding. Verify no stain on protected surfaces. Faster than setup (no taping/securing needed, just removal).

defect_tolerance.all: All protection materials removed. No tape residue on siding. No stain on protected surfaces. Site clean.

task_production_rates.name: Tool and Equipment Cleanup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Clean all staining equipment — flush sprayer if used (stain is thinner than paint, faster flush), clean brushes, pads, rollers, trays. Dispose of used abrasives and chemical containers. ~17 min. Stain cleanup is faster than paint cleanup (thinner product, easier flush).

defect_tolerance.all: All tools cleaned and stored. Sprayer flushed. Chemical containers properly disposed. Site debris removed.

factor_modifiers.name: Coating Type Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Coating type is the PRIMARY configuration dimension for deck specs (replaces quality_tier). Affects application rate — clear sealers are fastest (minimal working), solid stains are slowest (full film-build requiring more care). Material consumption handled separately by coverage profiles.
factor_modifiers.notes: Semi_transparent is baseline (1.00). Clear sealer is 20% faster (thin product, minimal working, wipe-on/wipe-off). Semi-solid is 10% slower (slight film-build, more care at lap lines). Solid stain is 25% slower (full film-build, requires even application for uniform appearance, runs/sags risk on vertical surfaces). Affects APPLICATION rate only — prep rates are not coating-type-dependent.

factor_modifiers.name: Wood Condition Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Wood condition drives prep intensity. New milled wood is baseline. Previously coated is slowest (stripping + sanding before recoat). Affects PREP tasks primarily — application rates are less affected because prep normalizes the surface.
factor_modifiers.notes: New milled is baseline (clean surface, mill glaze removal only). New PT seasoned is 5% slower (rough sawn texture, open grain already but PT chemical residue). Weathered is 50% slower (chemical restoration adds significant prep time, gray fiber removal, checking/splitting). Previously coated is 75% slower (stripping, sanding through old coating, adhesion testing, more chemical restoration steps). Applies to PREP tasks only — application tasks use coating_type modifier instead.

factor_modifiers.name: Wood Substrate Type Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Deck wood species affects prep and application rates. PT pine is baseline (~80% of residential decks). Cedar and redwood require tannin management (brightener step) and are slightly softer wood (easier to damage during prep).
factor_modifiers.notes: PT pine is baseline (dense, standard residential deck lumber). Cedar is 10% slower (softer wood requires lighter sanding pressure, tannin bleed-through adds brightener step, higher stain absorption on end grain). Redwood is 15% slower (similar to cedar plus even softer wood, more careful handling, premium material expectations). Applies to both prep and application tasks — cedar/redwood absorb more stain requiring slower application for even color.

quality_effects.description: Deck specs use coating_type as primary dimension instead of quality_tier. Coat count is driven by coating type, not tier.

clear_sealer.notes: Single coat of clear sealer. No interstage — one and done. Recoat in 1-2 years.

semi_transparent.notes: Two coats of semi-transparent stain. Second coat applied wet-on-wet or after 24 hr per product spec. No interstage inspection — penetrating product.

semi_solid.notes: Two coats of semi-solid stain. Slight film-build but still primarily penetrating. No interstage inspection.

solid_stain.notes: Two coats of solid stain. Film-forming — inspect between coats for holidays, runs, sags. Interstage inspection warranted because film defects are visible in final appearance.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: PT pine, semi-transparent, new milled — best case floor (spray_backbrush)
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Best case — baseline deck stain production. 275 SF/hr per 2-person crew.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: PT pine, clear sealer, new milled — fastest floor (spray_backbrush)
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Clear sealer on new PT pine — fastest possible deck production. 344 SF/hr per 2-person crew.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Cedar, semi-transparent, weathered — common refinish (brush floor)
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Cedar refinish with brush — common residential job. Substrate modifier only on application (wood_condition modifier applies to prep tasks). 114 SF/hr single worker.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Redwood, solid stain, previously coated — worst case floor (spray_backbrush)
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Solid stain on redwood — slowest application combination. 191 SF/hr per 2-person crew. Wood_condition modifier applies to prep tasks separately.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Redwood, solid stain, previously coated — worst case PREP (floor sand)
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Worst case prep — previously coated redwood. 25 SF/hr. Very slow but realistic for stripping old solid stain from softwood.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Maximum stacking check — solid stain × previously coated × redwood (application task)
modifier_stacking_examples.tasks_affected: TSK_DECK_STAIN_FLOOR_SPRAY_BACKBRUSH (if all 3 applied to same task)
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Absolute worst case with all 3 modifiers stacking (if wood_condition applied to application). 2.52x — well under 4.0x stacking cap. In practice, wood_condition primarily affects prep, so application stacking is typically coating_type × substrate_type only (max 1.44x).

assumptions: Base rates for spray_backbrush are per crew-hour with 2 workers (sprayer + brusher). crew_size = 2.
Base rates for brush, pad, and roll are per single worker. crew_size = 1.
Spray/backbrush coupling rule satisfied: spray rate <= backbrush rate (same combined rate). Back-brushing is MANDATORY for penetrating stains — spray alone prohibited.
Coating type replaces quality tier as primary configuration dimension. No QT-based rate scaling.
FAC_DECK_COATING_TYPE applies to APPLICATION tasks only. Prep rates are not coating-type-dependent.
FAC_DECK_WOOD_CONDITION applies to PREP tasks primarily. Application rates less affected because prep normalizes the surface.
FAC_DECK_SUBSTRATE_TYPE applies to both prep and application tasks (cedar/redwood stain absorption affects both).
Modifier stacking is multiplicative: effective_rate = base_rate / (coating_type × wood_condition × substrate_type).
Maximum combined modifier: 2.52x (solid_stain 1.25 × previously_coated 1.75 × redwood 1.15). Well under 4.0x stacking cap.
No FAC_EXT_ACCESS for deck floor — ground-level work. Elevated deck railings may require ladder but this is edge case not modeled.
Chemical restoration tasks (strip/brighten) are CONDITIONAL on wood_condition = weathered or previously_coated.
Seasoning verification is CONDITIONAL on new PT pine only.
Mill glaze sanding is CONDITIONAL on wood_condition = new.
Coat 2 tasks use same rate as coat 1 — penetrating stains still require same technique on second coat.
Stair step rate (3 EA/hr) includes alternating step pattern for access — effectively two passes across stair flight.
FIXED time tasks are not area-dependent. Deck size does not affect moisture testing, dwell times, or inspection fixed times.

Environmental modifiers (wind, sun, surface temp) are NOT declared as separate FAC_ entries for this spec — deck staining is ground-level work with different environmental sensitivities than wall coating. Hot sun causes stain to flash-dry but this is managed by SOP scheduling (early morning/late afternoon), not modifier.
Protection tasks use simple defect_tolerance (no QT split) because deck spec is not QT-driven.
risks: Solid stain on horizontal deck surfaces has the highest delamination risk of any coating configuration — horizontal surfaces trap moisture underneath film-forming coating. Flag for estimator review and customer disclosure.

Previously coated decks with unknown coating type require adhesion testing before committing to coating strategy — incompatible coatings (oil over latex or vice versa) will delaminate. May require full strip regardless.
Chemical restoration (strip + brighten) adds significant time and a separate mobilization day (24-48 hr dry time). Estimator must account for return visit.
Cedar/redwood tannin bleed can occur through semi-transparent and clear coatings — not a defect but requires customer expectation setting.
Spindle staining rates are highly variable — turned spindles can be 2-3x slower than square spindles. 12 EA/hr is a mixed average.
Stair step rate (3 EA/hr) assumes standard tread+riser. Wrapped stringers or complex stair geometry would be significantly slower.
Deck floor spray_backbrush rate (275 SF/hr) assumes clear working area. Railing posts interrupting floor spray pattern reduce effective rate.
Wood condition modifier for previously_coated (1.75x) assumes standard stripping difficulty. Epoxy-fortified or multi-layer old coatings may exceed this modifier — flag for estimator review.
validation_plan: Time 3 spray_backbrush floor staining jobs on new PT pine to calibrate 275 SF/hr baseline per 2-person crew.
Time 2 brush-only floor staining jobs to calibrate 125 SF/hr baseline.
Time 2 pad applicator floor jobs to calibrate 250 SF/hr baseline.
Track railing brush staining time per LF on 3 jobs to validate 10 LF/hr baseline.
Track spindle staining time: compare square vs turned spindles to validate mixed 12 EA/hr average.
Time 2 chemical restoration sequences (strip + brighten + rinse) to validate combined prep time on weathered decks.
Track stair step staining with alternating pattern to validate 3 EA/hr rate including access logistics.
Compare clear sealer vs solid stain application times on same deck area to validate FAC_DECK_COATING_TYPE modifier spread (0.80x to 1.25x).
Track furniture staging and return times across 5 jobs to validate FIXED time ranges.
Compare PT pine vs cedar staining rates on similar deck geometry to validate FAC_DECK_SUBSTRATE_TYPE 1.10x modifier.
